what_its_for: Bumetanide is a 'water pill' (diuretic) that helps your kidneys remove extra salt and water from your body through your urine. It is used to reduce swelling (edema) caused by heart failure, liver disease, or kidney disease. Removing this extra fluid helps reduce swelling in your legs, ankles, feet, and belly, and makes it easier to breathe.
how_to_take: Take bumetanide by mouth with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk. Because this medicine makes you urinate more often, try to take it in the morning or early afternoon so it does not keep you up at night. If you take it twice a day, take the second dose no later than mid-afternoon. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition and how your body responds. A common starting dose for adults is 0.5 mg to 2 mg taken once daily, but your doctor may adjust this. Never change your dose on your own. Always follow the instructions on your prescription label.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still earlier in the day. If it is already late in the afternoon or evening, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time the following morning. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store bumetanide at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date on the bottle.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and increase dizziness. Be careful when standing up quickly from sitting or lying down, as this medicine can cause dizziness or lightheadedness. Avoid becoming dehydrated — do not limit your fluid intake unless your doctor tells you to. Talk to your doctor before using salt substitutes or potassium supplements, as this medicine can affect your electrolyte levels. Avoid prolonged time in the sun without protection, as bumetanide may make your skin more sensitive to sunlight.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: severe muscle cramps, weakness, or pain; irregular or fast heartbeat; feeling very dizzy or faint; confusion or unusual drowsiness; little or no urination; severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea; signs of dehydration such as extreme thirst or dry mouth; ringing in your ears or sudden hearing loss; or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: Bumetanide starts working within 30 to 60 minutes after you take it. You will likely notice that you are urinating more frequently for about 2 to 3 hours after each dose. Swelling may begin to decrease within the first day or two of treatment. It is important to keep taking this medicine even if you feel better, as it helps control your condition over time.
special_populations: Older adults: You may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine, including dizziness and electrolyte changes. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if bumetanide passes into breast milk. Ask your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medicine. Kidney or liver disease: Use this medicine with caution. Your doctor will monitor you closely and may adjust your dose. Children: This medicine is not commonly recommended for children. Only give it to a child if prescribed by a doctor.
